purpose: Every declared digest in the pinned corpora, with the byte scope the corpus's own governing document names for it. Read by tools/walk-digests.ts, which recomputes each one and reports match / mismatch / unregistered / serializer_disagreement.

how_to_read.rules: Each rule names ONE scope, taken from a document by line number, and the walker expands it deterministically over the corpus bytes. A rule is one entry per (corpus, field kind) rather than per concrete field: the concrete fields are an enumeration of bytes, the scope is the claim, and only the claim can be reviewed against a document. Every concrete field a rule expands to appears as its own row in walker/report.json.
how_to_read.unregistered: Concrete digest-shaped fields no rule covers, listed by JSON pointer with the reason. They are counted and printed, never silently skipped, and they do not fail the run: an unrecomputable field is not a wrong field.

status.declared: the cited document states this scope for this field
status.inferred: the document is silent; the scope is taken from the corpus's own self-description (a header member, a description string, or the fixture generator) and that source is named

evidence-action-spec.note: Corpus-internal normative document, not an IETF draft in refs/. Cited as the owning document for the evidence.action/0 format because it is the only document that states these scopes.

rules.scope_source: the corpus's own header members: version 2, canonicalization "RFC 8785 JCS", hash_algorithm "SHA-256". marques-08 cites this corpus but does not define its schema.
same corpus header; each vector's own description states the digest is over its canonical form.

rules.construction: sha256(jcs({payload,signature,anchors} of this vector's originating envelope))

which_envelope.1: the vector named by originating_envelope_ref, when the vector carries one (happy_path, base64url_tolerance)
which_envelope.2: the vector's own input, when that input is itself the three-key envelope (envelope_byte_equality, whose description reads 'A's full signed envelope ({payload, signature, anchors})')
which_envelope.3: otherwise the file's single declared originating envelope -- the vector whose input is a three-key object and whose description declares it to be A's full signed envelope and says 'Base64 of the digest is the value B places in counterparty_binding.envelope_hash on the happy-path vector'. This covers opaque_receipt_ref and transport_label_non_trust, which vary one non-envelope member and name no envelope of their own.
which_envelope.4: otherwise unregistered: no envelope can be resolved, and guessing one would manufacture a result
which_envelope.status_note: Resolution steps 1 and 2 are read from the corpus's structure; step 3 is read from the corpus's description strings and is therefore inferred, not declared. The DIGEST SCOPE is declared throughout (marques-08 s5.7); only the identity of A's envelope is resolved this way.

rules.encoding: per field suffix: envelope_hash and envelope_hash_base64 base64, envelope_hash_hex hex, envelope_hash_base64url base64url
rules.quote: Base64-encoded SHA-256 digest computed over A's entire serialized signed envelope, including A's signature bytes ... the envelope is the three-key object {"payload", "signature", "anchors"} ... B MUST NOT re-canonicalize A's payload or strip the anchors array before computing the digest.

alt_scope.note: The -09 forward scope. Recomputed and reported for information; never used to decide match/mismatch, because -08 as it reads today is the graded text (the author's instruction of 2026-09-02 13:07:20Z, recorded in FINDINGS.md A5).

rules.quote: populated with the lowercase hex encoding of SHA-256(JCS(R)), where R is the payload member of the immediately prior receipt ... the digest covers R, NOT the envelope object

rules.construction: sha256(jcs(whole receipt object of verifier/conformance-vectors/acta-02-chain-link/predecessor.json, signature included))
rules.quote: The previousReceiptHash field MUST be the lowercase hex encoding of SHA-256(JCS(receipt)), where receipt is the entire signed receipt object including the signature field.

rules.construction: sha256(jcs(sibling receipt.json minus the signature member))
rules.quote: 5.6. Signature Scope ... signature field removed prior to canonicalization. The signature field MUST be removed from the object, not set to null or to the empty string.

rules.construction: sha256(jcs(whole predecessor receipt object, signature included))
sha256(jcs(whole predecessor receipt object, signature included))

rules.scope_source: These are OUR fixtures, generated by tools/make-acta-fixtures.mjs, and the directory name declares which scope each chain was built under. The marques payload scope is registered here because that is what the fixture exists to exercise; registering it under farley's whole-receipt scope would manufacture a mismatch the corpus never claimed. FINDINGS.md E2/E3 and test/acta.test.ts record the split.
rules.note: Document lines given for the scope itself; the ASSIGNMENT of this scope to this directory is inferred, not declared.

rules.scope_source: Directory name declares a third scope (the signing input) that no document in refs/ defines as a chain-digest scope. Left unrecomputed rather than guessed.

rules.construction: sha256(raw bytes of the mapping document under fixtures/verification-state/mappings/ whose digest it names)
rules.encoding: sha256-prefixed hex (the corpus writes the separator as '-', e.g. sha256-0a78...)
rules.quote: Receipts MUST bind to a content-addressed mapping via the v_gate_mapping_hash field (SHA-256) ... Verifier implementations MUST verify the SHA-256 digest of the fetched mapping document against v_gate_mapping_hash before use
rules.note: Content-addressed by construction: a value is recomputable here only when the document it addresses is in the corpus. Values naming a document this repository does not hold are reported unregistered with that reason, never as a mismatch -- there is nothing to disagree with.

rules.construction: "sha256:" + hex(sha256(jcs({v: <the record's own v token>, session_id: <the record's session_id>, marker: "genesis"})))
"sha256:" + hex(sha256(jcs(record N-1 minus its sig member)))
"sha256:" + hex(sha256(jcs(the last non-checkpoint record minus its sig member)))
"sha256:" + hex(sha256(jcs({v: <the record's own v token>, session_id: <the record's session_id>, marker: "genesis"})))
rules.scope_source: These chains declare v="evidence.action/1", one version on from the evidence.action/0 corpus SPEC.md governs. No delivery-specific document states a scope, so the /0 constructions are applied with the record's OWN v token substituted into the genesis object, which is what the SPEC's genesis form means by the format version. Marked inferred because applying a /0 document to a /1 corpus is an inference, not a declaration.

rules.construction: "sha256:" + hex(sha256(jcs(record N-1 minus its sig member)))
"sha256:" + hex(sha256(jcs(the last non-checkpoint record minus its sig member)))

corpora.corpus_note: Every digest-shaped value in this corpus is a 0x-prefixed 32-byte EVM word (keccak-256 transaction hashes, gate request hashes, reason-code hashes) produced by on-chain contracts and by Insight's own gate service. No document in refs/ governs them, the preimages are not in the corpus, and they are not SHA-256-over-JCS at all. All are unregistered.

cpb/ holds TypeScript sources and Markdown result tables, no JSON corpus data. Its digest-shaped tokens are 64-hex strings inside prose and code, not fields of a document the walker can address by JSON pointer. Counted as non-field tokens in the report, not registered.
